name: Permanent Resident Status -- Five-Year Continuous Residence

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 5 years of continuous lawful residence, with every day covered by a valid, unexpired work permit, student permit, dependant/spousal permit, or business permit -- even brief gaps reset the clock.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 5 years of unbroken, continuously-permitted residence.

requirements.blocker_text: Must not fall under the Immigration Act's 'prohibited immigrants' classification.

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: no continuous absence of 2+ years, or PR may be revoked

sources.title: Martin George & Company (immigration law firm) -- Permanent Resident Status in Trinidad and Tobago: The Five-Year Continuous Residence Route: Immigration Act Chapter 18:01 Section 14, ministerial discretion, permissible permit types, 18-48 month realistic processing time, revocation grounds

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Trinidad and Tobago's initial build. STATUS: DRAFT -- the Ministry of Homeland Security's own PR application page (homelandsecurity.gov.tt/faq/faq-5/) confirms the Citizenship and Residency Unit exists and links to a separate application-procedure page, but does not itself state the 5-year figure, criteria, or legal citation; this file is instead sourced to a tier-3 immigration law firm's detailed article. Notably, the source states PR approval is fully discretionary -- 'no automatic right exists' even after 5 years of qualifying residence -- a materially different framing from most PR routes in this dataset, where meeting stated criteria is presented as sufficient. citizenship_after_months (60) reflects the same source's statement that naturalisation becomes available after holding PR status for 5 years -- see tt_naturalisation.json, whose own tier-1 Citizenship Act source independently confirms a 12-months-immediately-preceding-plus-5-of-7-years formula; the two figures are consistent in substance even though sourced separately.
